source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 5 (Measures of Central Tendency).

sections.heading: 1. Central Tendency — Meaning
points: A **measure of central tendency** = a single value that represents the whole data (a typical/central value).
The three main measures: **Mean, Median, Mode**.

sections.heading: 2. Arithmetic Mean (Average)
points: **Mean = sum of all values ÷ number of values** (ΣX/N).
For grouped data, use assumed mean / step-deviation methods.
**Merits:** based on all values, easy to compute; **Demerits:** affected by **extreme values (outliers)**; cannot be found graphically.
**Weighted mean** — gives different weights to items by importance.

sections.heading: 3. Median
points: **Median** = the **middle value** when data is arranged in order (positional average); half the values lie below it.
For N odd = the (N+1)/2 th item; for grouped data, a formula is used.
**Merits:** not affected by extreme values; can be found graphically (ogive).
**Related positional measures:** **quartiles, deciles, percentiles**.

sections.heading: 4. Mode
points: **Mode** = the value that occurs **most frequently** in the data.
**Merits:** easy to understand, unaffected by extreme values, useful for qualitative data.
**Demerits:** may not be well-defined (no mode or multiple modes).
**Relationship (empirical):** **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** (for moderately skewed distributions).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three measures: Mean, Median, Mode.
Mean = ΣX/N (affected by extreme values).
Median = middle value (positional; not affected by extremes; found via ogive).
Mode = most frequently occurring value.
Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **mean is affected by extreme values (outliers)**; the **median and mode are not**.
**Median = middle value**; **Mode = most frequent value**.
**Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.
The **median can be found graphically** using an ogive.
